lens: time and evaluation: interruptible waits and wake-on-event, auto standing orders, notices, temporal evaluation and sampling, multi-phase episodes and the harness done protocol, clock / calendar / DST, savepoints, long-horizon cost, determinism and replay

findings.title: wait(until) / watch / person_enters-leaves notices use room-mode visibility: they fire on, and name, things and people the robot does not perceive (dark rooms, unidentified people, geometric camera facing away), and the acceptance of a wait is a who-is-here oracle by id in the dark
findings.evidence: house_sim/kernel/timeline.py: perceivable() (122-149) falls back to watch_condition_visible (57-93), whose entity rule is Perception(None).visible (96-98, room-mode set: a dark shape counts) plus the glance-tier check on the TRUE field (73), and whose people rule is only 'location == robot room' (90-92); _agent_notice (558-571) and _source_perceived (312-327) use the room-mode seen_dark rule even when robot.view exists. Probes (scratch %SCRATCH%/t1_reviewC_time/): probe2.py (gen-2 house seed 0, camera geometric, both perception modes): after face deg=180 the observation lists no people, yet wait(600, until people.resident_1.posture == sitting) returns 'Waited 90 s (until condition met)' at the scripted change, an auto watch on the same condition runs 'announce ok', and wait(interrupt_on person_enters) returns 'interrupted: person_enters in living_room_1 from resident_2' with obs.notices source 'resident_2' while obs.people is empty. Room mode, realistic, lights off (fixture of tests/test_timeline.py): the only record is {'label': 'dark shape'} with no 'open' field, but wait(until entities.<that handle>.open is_true) ends 'Waited 60 s (until condition met)' exactly when the scripted door opens; wait(until people.<dark person handle>.posture == sitting) ends at 90 s. Identity oracle: in the same dark room ask('resident_1') is refused 'It is too dark to tell who is who here', but wait(1, until people.resident_1.posture ...) is accepted and wait(1, until people.resident_2.posture ...) (resident_2 in room_3) is refused 'Wait only on what the robot can observe'. C-MERGE listed the geometric part as a known gap; the room-mode dark / privacy / identity cases are the same root cause and are not covered by any test or by G4 (the perception audit never issues until / watch conditions).
findings.fix: Make timeline.perceivable realism- and camera-aware per referenced id (TIER1_INTEGRATION 1.3): with realistic perception an entity path is perceivable only when the id is in perception.perceived_ids(env) (geometric: the cached step view; refreshed at a substep only for the ids the waiting rule references, via camera.can_see, to keep the 0.02 ms budget) AND realism currently grants the field at its tier (a dark-spell shape grants nothing); a person / pet path needs the robot's room lit, body.imaging and the agent identified (realism identity, not a dark-spell shape; geometric: detected and identified in the view) -- refuse the wait/watch with the same DARK_WHO / FAR_WHO wording realism.inbound uses, so acceptance leaks nothing. Apply the same per-id test in _agent_notice / _source_perceived (geometric: the camera's detection, not seen_dark) and never set 'source' otherwise. Add perception_audit checks that issue until/watch on unseen ids and on dark shapes (expect identical refusals for present and absent people).

findings.title: Nothing can wake a waiting robot when the smoke alarms sound: no alarm notices are posted, alarm_state is not observable for until/watch, yet the wait doc and the LLM system prompt tell agents to rely on interrupt_on=['urgent'] for unattended waits
findings.evidence: Probe probe9.py: A-d9e7a4d5d112d2-01 seed 0 (burnt toast) with the notice bus on; after 120 s all six detectors are alarm_state 'alarm', including fixture_3 in the robot's room, and obs.sounds lists a 95 dB temporal-3 alarm 'this room', but wait(seconds=120, interrupt_on=['urgent','alarm','any_sound']) returns 'Waited 120 s' and state.notices == []. wait(until entities.fixture_3.alarm_state == 'alarm') is refused (alarm_state is not in timeline.OBSERVABLE_FIELDS, 48-49; no domain extends it: grep), in realistic mode every alarm field is refused, and the oracle-accepted 'alarm' / 'beeping' fields do not exist on detectors (never true). Agent-facing text: timeline.py 609-610 'pass interrupt_on=["urgent"] for unattended waits' and eval/llm.py 443 'pass interrupt_on ["urgent"] for long unattended waits'. The handoff's known gap ('until then interrupt_on urgent hears only addressed speech') defers it to the adoption round, but the safety domain's alarms, the kernel's own sounds channel and the 'urgent' advice all exist now, so an honest agent following the docs sleeps through a fire alarm and is then failed by the spec.
findings.fix: Bridge it in the kernel now (TIME-EVAL's timeline.py): in derive_notices, detect rising edges of alarm-like entity states (alarm_state in ('alarm','test'), beeping true, audible_status changes) over a w.static_index of entities that have those fields (O(detectors) per substep) and post w.notice('alarm', source=eid, room=root_room, db=entity.get('alarm_db', 85)) through robot_perceives; add alarm_state (glance tier) to OBSERVABLE_FIELDS so until/watch can test it; keep the domain follow-up for richer kinds (smoke visual, CO, appliance chimes). Until the bridge lands, remove the 'urgent' advice from the wait doc and the LLM prompt. Test: the safety spec above with interrupt_on=['urgent'] ends at the first alarm boundary (30 s).

findings.title: A wait or standing order on a person or pet leaving the robot's room is accepted but can never fire; one on a person arriving is refused, so 'when X leaves / comes in' standing orders cannot be expressed
findings.evidence: timeline.watch_condition_visible 90-92 makes people/pets paths perceivable only while that agent is in the robot's room, so the moment the condition 'not here' becomes true it stops being perceivable. Probe probe5.py (both perception modes, lit room, door open): resident_1 leaves at t=60; wait(600, until people.resident_1.location ne room_1) and the {not: {eq room_1}} form both return 'Waited 600 s | noticed: person_leaves in room_1 from resident_1' (the robot noticed the departure, the until never ended the wait); watch(mode auto) on the same condition stays fired False after the wait. A first version of probe8.py: watch(people.resident_2.location == robot room) while resident_2 is in the kitchen is refused 'Watch only conditions the robot can observe'. The absence of a person from a lit room the robot is in is as observable as their presence; tests/test_timeline.py test_a_condition_the_robot_stops_perceiving_does_not_end_the_wait pins the opposite.
findings.fix: In perceivable, treat a people/pets 'location' comparison whose operand is (or excludes) the robot's current room as an observation of the robot's own room: perceivable when the robot can see its room (lit, body.imaging; geometric: room coverage of the step view) or hear footsteps (body.can_hear full), whether or not the agent is in it now; keep conditions about other rooms refused. Evaluate perceivability per atomic predicate inside not/any (an 'any' with one perceivable true branch can fire). Add tests for 'until X leaves', 'watch until X comes in' and a realistic dark-room refusal.

findings.title: Milestones and response obligations reached by an action are stamped at the action's START: deadlines and within_s windows are met by actions that finish after them (a regression from the legacy end-of-step time)
findings.evidence: engine.step samples the monitor at 'action' (481) before _advance; Monitor.sample stamps t = state.time_s (412) = the step start. HEAD recorded milestones after _advance (git show HEAD:house_sim/kernel/engine.py 482-489, _update_milestones 628-634). Probe probe4.py: generated house seed 0, task milestones {'there': robot.room == master_bedroom_1}, deadlines {'there': 5}: go_to takes 0.0 -> 20.428 s ('Arrived at master_bedroom_1'), the milestone is recorded at time_s 0.0 and evaluate() says success True, failures [] (HEAD: milestone 20.428 > 5, deadline:there). The same applies to responses (an obligation is met at the start of a 240 s repot or a long walk) and to order: [[a, b]]. The handoff states it as deviation 5; TIER1_SWEEP 8.2's purpose was that a milestone 'records its true time', and the completion of an action is at its end.
findings.fix: Keep the 'action' sample for never/always (latching what the handler did), but stamp milestones, counted-milestone times, held_for starts and response met times reached at that sample with the action's completion time (state.time_s + the step's own seconds, known before _advance; for auto commands now + spent), or defer those edges to the first substep sample at or after that time. Re-run the 7 milestone specs (S-R1) and add a test: a 20 s walk does not meet a 5 s deadline.

findings.title: decided says 'fail' because of a superseded (unscored) phase while the episode succeeds; schema-3 idle verification stops on it
findings.evidence: monitor.Monitor.decided (581-605) returns 'fail' for any latched violation (585), any missed obligation (587) and missed deadlines of every phase in phase_times (589), including a phase that ended 'superseded' (scored False), while evaluate()'s failures only count episode-level labels and scored phases. Probe probe3.py (tests/test_phases.py SPEC + p2 never facts.urgent + p3 when facts.urgent supersedes p2): after p3 starts, violations {'never:p2/calm': 7262.0}; after 'stopping' and phase_done: success True, failures [], decided 'fail'. verify._early_exit (48-51) stops a schema-3 idle run on decided == 'fail', so such a spec's idle check can end early and report idle_fails without waiting out the budget.
findings.fix: In Monitor.decided count only labels of the episode level and of phases that are active, pending or ended with scored True: pass the PhaseController (or the set of superseded phase ids) in and skip 'never:<id>/', 'always:<id>/', 'response:<id>/' labels and phase deadlines of superseded phases. Add the probe as a test (success True implies decided None).

findings.title: On generation-2 houses (the schema-3 default) the agent's clock reads DST wall time while every domain runs on standard time: the house's own clocks and the residents' schedules are an hour off what the agent sees, and {'by': 'HH:MM'} deadlines are wall time
findings.evidence: clock.describe (121-130) shows wall(state) on clock model 2; people schedules use clock.hour / now (systems/people/common.py 255-277, standard time), electrical clock displays use C.local_seconds (systems/electrical/clocks.py 35-37), admin_inventory curb days clock.now. Probe: generate_house(0, gen=2) (clock model 2, region ca, start 2026-10-09T10:00): obs.time {'datetime': '2026-10-09T11:00', 'hour': 11.0, 'dst': True}, people hour 10.0, alarm_clock_1 displays '10:00 AM'. The default start dates fall inside DST for us/ca/uk/eu, so every gen-2 episode shows the mismatch; parse_when / deadline 'by' (390-427) interprets HH:MM as wall time while a resident who 'wakes at 07:00' does so at 07:00 standard = 08:00 wall. Only electrical's 'DST-aware clocks' is listed as a follow-up (TIER1_INTEGRATION 6); people, admin_inventory and climate schedules are not.
findings.fix: Either gate DST behind an explicit clock flag (clock.dst: true) that the generator sets only after the domains move to wall time, or add one kernel helper clock.local_hour(state) / local_now(state) (= wall on model 2) and switch the people schedules, electrical clock displays, admin_inventory day boundaries and any 'HH:MM' authored times to it in the same change; add people, admin_inventory and climate to the adoption-round list; test that obs.time, displayed clocks and a resident's 07:00 wake agree on a gen-2 house in October.

findings.title: Hidden weather bookkeeping (weather.process.seed_key, forecast_state, override_until_s) is readable through wait(until) / watch: every weather.* path counts as perceivable
findings.evidence: timeline._perceivable 147-148 returns _weather_perceivable(w) for any 'weather' head, before and instead of the realistic checks; perception.WEATHER_HIDDEN (65) hides exactly these keys from obs.weather. Probe (gen-2 house seed 0, oracle and realistic): obs.weather has no 'process', but wait(60, until weather.process.model == 'normals_v1') -> 'Waited 0 s (until condition met)', the 'other' value waits 60 s, and until weather.process.seed_key startswith 'wx-2' -> 'Waited 0 s (until condition met)' (a 0-cost prefix oracle: the seed key determines the whole future weather, the leak GEN's handoff 7 warned about); watch on weather.process.region is accepted. Through a window without network the rule also accepts numeric thresholds on temperature_c / wind_mps in realistic mode.
findings.fix: In _perceivable, for weather.* require the second path component to be a perceived weather field (not in perception.WEATHER_HIDDEN, not '_'-prefixed); through a window (no network) allow only condition / rain / snow comparisons without numeric ops in realistic mode; with the network allow what a weather app shows. Add a perception_audit check issuing until/watch on every WEATHER_HIDDEN key.

findings.title: A phase's deadlines (and per-phase milestones) are satisfied by milestones reached in earlier phases
findings.evidence: compile_task (174-180) compiles a phase's milestones into the global namespace with no window; Monitor.add (351-354) refuses a second definition of the same name; missed_deadlines (543-545) compares the global first time with the phase limit. Probe: tests/test_phases.py SPEC with p2 milestones {'ready_p2': said('ready')} and deadlines {'ready_p2': 60}; the robot says 'ready' in phase 1 (t=0) and never in phase 2: milestone ready_p2 {'time_s': 0.0}, p2 limit 7264.0, phase records [('p1', True, []), ('p2', True, [])]. The handoff lists 'per-phase milestones share the global namespace' as a known gap, but the consequence (phase deadlines pass vacuously, the 'same task again tomorrow' recipe of TIER1_SWEEP 23 cannot be scored) is not stated.
findings.fix: Compile a phase's milestones as '<id>/<name>' sampled only inside the phase window (after phase:<id>:start), resolve the phase's deadlines, order and response triggers against that namespace first, and allow the same name in several phases; keep top-level milestones global.

findings.title: Auto standing orders stall silently inside waits: an order whose firing interrupts the wait never runs in it, and after the per-step 500-command budget no order runs for the rest of a multi-day wait
findings.evidence: engine._advance (725-737) breaks on wait.check() before _run_orders, and the 'order' notice is posted at fire time (timeline.fire_orders 772). Probe: watch(time_s >= 100, announce, mode auto) then wait(600, interrupt_on=['order','urgent']) -> 'Waited 120 s (interrupted: order in room_1)', the order stays due and nothing was announced; after two more actions it is still due (it runs only at the next wait). Budget: 25 auto orders x 20 commands firing at t=100 plus one order on time_s >= 3600, then wait(7200): the message ends 'auto orders paused (order budget)', the 3600 s order is left due with nothing said, and the wait runs on to 7226 s; in a 7-day wait this disables every auto order for days. The 'standing orders ran' note (wait_message 921-926) is not capped (500 entries in one message), unlike the 10-notice note. TIER1_SWEEP 6.4: 'when the order fires during an idle advance, the engine runs its commands at that substep'.
findings.fix: At an interrupting boundary run the due auto orders first and end the wait after them (or post the 'order' notice when its commands ran); make the budget per simulated hour of an idle advance (or end the wait with reason 'auto orders paused' so the agent regains control); cap the order note like the notice note ('+N more').

findings.title: Idle verification still stops after 30 x 3600 s = 30 h, so long-horizon specs (multi-day budgets, per-phase budgets over 30 h) are never waited out
findings.evidence: tasks/verify.py _wait_out (54-64): chunk = min(3600, remaining) and max_steps=30, used for the task budget and for each phase budget; wait accepts 604800 s. A spec with time_budget_s 604800 (the sweep's week-long weather recipe V-68a0baf1a10293-01) is idle-checked for 108000 s only, so a spec satisfied by doing nothing for 3 days passes verification. Pre-existing loop (HEAD idle 32-42), rewritten by this package; no authored spec exceeds 30 h yet (scan of tasks/authored).
findings.fix: chunk = min(604800, max(3600, ceil(remaining / 30))) (still at most 30 steps, so step budgets are unaffected), applied to the episode and to each phase budget; add a test with a 3-day budget whose idle run must reach time_s == budget.

findings.title: A contingent phase (start when / supersedes) that never starts makes the episode unwinnable, keeps the harness 'waiting', and the evaluation names no episode-level failure
findings.evidence: PhaseController.evaluate (310-312) scores phases not started as failed ('not_started', scored True); waiting (259-267) keeps the harness episode alive for them. Probe: tests/test_phases.py SPEC + p3 {start: {when: facts.urgent}, supersedes: p2} with no urgent event: p1 and p2 succeed, phase_done says 'the next request comes later' {'waiting': True}, evaluate(): success False, failures [], phases [('p1', True), ('p2', True), ('p3', False, ['not_started'])]. TIER1_SWEEP 9 describes 'when' phases as exogenous interruptions that may happen; nothing lets an author mark one optional.
findings.fix: Add an 'optional': true phase key (lint: only with a when / at_s start): an optional phase that has not started when the episode is evaluated is unscored and does not keep the harness waiting; list 'phase_failed:<id>' / 'phase_not_started:<id>' in the episode failures.

verified_ok: Save -> load -> continue equals a continuous run (state digest, evaluation, step messages, Mind dump) for oracle/realistic x room/geometric at four save points of a script with listening waits, person_enters/leaves interrupts, an auto standing order that ran inside a wait and a response obligation (probe8.py, 16/16 equal).

TIER1_INTEGRATION 1.9 order is implemented as written: action sample after settle_energy and the physics settle; substep = systems (probes) -> events -> settle -> orders -> notices -> monitor -> phase tick -> wait check -> auto orders -> trim_touched; each auto command runs under a savepoint in 'covered' mode, is settled as an action, released, sampled ('order') and then advances the world.

World savepoints (rollback_to / release): layers restored in reverse, quiet field journals, touch-log truncation with consumer-cursor clamping, phys_scratch and the heard-notice buffer restored; a refused auto command leaves no notice, order-log or state trace beyond the logged refusal.

Monitor footprints: every journaled write path feeds _touched / _touched_sections / _quiet_touched; begin() resets the monitor cursor; predicates not evaluated at the previous sample are re-evaluated; type narrowing is safe (no code changes an existing entity's type in place: only fresh portion records set 'type').

Darkness and hearing for kernel notices: person_enters / person_leaves in a dark room are heard without a source (probe1.py); battery / fault notices come from detected events only (the body review's latent-fault note is honored).

Long horizon: one 7-day wait on a gen-2 house completes with bounded memory (tracemalloc peak 2.7 MB), capped notices / event_log; quiet-day CPU 6.73 s plain vs 6.69 s with the bus and a listening wait vs 6.81 s with a monitor (gen-2 seed 0), i.e. TIME-EVAL's own overhead is within about 1-2 %; tools/sweep_bench.py all ok (notices 0.0015 ms, until 0.0005 ms, monitor_idle 0.0027 ms, monitor_quant 0.031 ms, calendar 0.34 ms).

Calendar data: 26 spot checks 2026-2027 (US observed Friday/Monday incl. Dec 31 for New Year 2028, UK and Ontario substitute days, JP citizens' holiday 2026-09-22 and substitutes 2026-05-06 / 2027-03-22, German Ascension / Whit Monday / Unity Day, Ontario Victoria / Family / Thanksgiving) all correct; DST bounds in standard time correct for us/ca (fall-back at 01:00 standard, wall 01:00-01:59 repeated), uk (01:00 GMT) and eu (02:00 CET); parse_when resolves the spring-forward gap and the fall-back repeat sensibly.

Phases: a phase that ends on time inside a wait starts its successor inside the same wait when the gap is due, otherwise at the end of the step; the harness calls on_request for env-started phases and replay_log replays phase_done steps; supersedes closes the phase unscored in evaluate().
Default wait and queue-mode watch unchanged (state digests in the gate; probe7 plain wait cost).

The package's six test files pass (python -m unittest tests.test_timeline tests.test_world_savepoint tests.test_monitor tests.test_phases tests.test_clock tests.test_predicates_v3: 114 tests OK, 39.5 s), covering fire-time realism for queue orders (S-R2), max_runs / cooldown / expiry, forbidden auto commands and the probes-on / probes-off digest equality.
notes: Reviewer lens: TIME & EVALUATION (TIME-EVAL as merged at C-MERGE, with PEOPLE-IO's renderings where they carry time data). Read TIER1_SWEEP (6, 8, 9, 10.1, 11.1, 16, 18-22), TIER1_INTEGRATION (1.3, 1.8, 1.9, 1.17, 2.5, 3, 5), TIER1_DECISIONS and every handoff_*.md (TIME-EVAL, PEOPLE-IO in full; gate usage from handoff_TIER1-GATE.md). Probes are in the scratch folder t1_reviewC_time/ (probe1.py ... probe10.py and inline runs quoted in the evidence) and drove HouseEnv.step with handles from observations in both perception modes and both cameras; no project file was edited except this JSON. Already-known items re-verified and kept because they remain open: finding 1 (C-MERGE known gap, extended here to room-mode darkness, dark shapes and the identity oracle), finding 2 (TIME-EVAL known gap 'notices nobody posts yet', raised to high because the wait doc and the LLM prompt promise it), finding 8 (TIME-EVAL known gap on the milestone namespace; the deadline consequence is new). Observed but not raised (other lens or by design): a heard speech notice from the next room withholds the words while obs.messages (people domain heard_by_robot) carries the full text and speaker id; substeps are aligned to the step start, so a system-made change can be stamped up to 30 s later depending on earlier action durations (inherent to the 30 s substep, no regression); auto orders do not run during listen and held orders wait for the next wait (documented).
